questions.question: Name three factors that make a solid dissolve faster.
questions.expected_answer: A solid dissolves faster when the solvent is hotter, when the mixture is stirred or shaken, and when the solute is in smaller pieces, like icing sugar instead of a sugar cube.

questions.question: Use particles to explain why hot water and stirring make sugar dissolve faster.
questions.expected_answer: In hot water the particles move faster and bump harder and more often into the sugar, so they pull sugar particles away and carry them off more quickly. Stirring moves the very sugary water away from the grains and brings fresh water to them, and spreads the grains so water can reach all sides.

questions.question: Describe a fair test to find out whether grain size affects the rate of dissolving.
questions.expected_answer: Use three glasses with the same amount of water at the same temperature. Put the same mass of sugar in each, as a cube, as ordinary sugar and as icing sugar. Stir each one in the same way and time how long each takes to dissolve. Only the grain size changes. The icing sugar dissolves fastest and the cube slowest, because smaller pieces have more surface touching the water.
